cruise_gap.limitations: Gap-only numerical controls on one synthetic flight; no full00:11 recovery or general convergence claim

cruise_interval_proposals.scope: Synthetic first-gap comparisons; no full-flight stability claim

conditions: Numerical source inclusion is a sensitivity diagnostic, not a physical observation or confidence interval.
Each case is renormalized on the selected cruise sources and, for drift, native model support before the same initial case probabilities are assigned.
Drift and search likelihoods are unchanged. The all-sources calculations reproduce the saved mixtures.
Source influence combines each cruise run with its sampled terminal descendants; this does not separately identify cruise versus terminal sampling error.
Leaving sources out cannot detect trajectories missed by every original run. Independent synthetic recovery remains necessary.

exchange.scope: Independent saved-data check of helper targets, exchange balance and cold output. Short dependent chains do not establish convergence, recovery or a calibrated MH370 posterior.

independent_checks.scope: Dependent Markov chains; descriptive exploration diagnostics, not convergence, burn-in certification or new independent MH370 trajectories.

methods:
We estimate where MH370 could have struck the ocean by simulating aircraft motion, comparing predicted satellite measurements with observations, and updating candidate probabilities. Satellite timing (BTO) constrains range; frequency shifts (BFO) constrain motion. We first estimate flights through 00:11 UTC, then simulate their continuation to impact. The cruise ensemble began with 1.02 million candidates, allowing up to 16 changes of direction, eight changes of speed and eight changes of altitude. Commanded speeds span Mach 0.73–0.84 (73–84% of sound speed) and altitudes 25,000–43,000 feet. Distributions of manoeuvre times and control modes are modelling choices. For Bayesian prediction and updating, see Davey et al. (2016, Section 3.1). Fuel exhaustion is conditional on 00:15–00:19 UTC; fuel burn uses a public approximation awaiting aircraft-specific validation. Each independent terminal run selects 12,288 weighted states from that pool.

The final log-on produced two transmissions, labelled R600 and R1200. Their BFOs may be unreliable. We compare four cases: neither, R600 only, R1200 only, or both usable without extra oscillator warm-up adjustments. All retain the corrected R600 BTO and an airborne transmitter through 00:19:37.443. Each separately fitted case receives an initial weight of 25%, before drift/search updates. This specifies a mixture of conditional estimates; it does not infer instrument reliability from the BFO fit scores.

Let q_m(x) be the normalized impact density for case m, a_m=1/4 its initial weight, L_d(x) the debris-drift likelihood, and L_s(x) the probability searches would miss wreckage at x. The equations below update both locations and case probabilities. Set L_d=1 for flight-only results and L_s=1 before searches. This follows Bayesian conditioning and model averaging (Hoeting et al., 1999, p.383).

Drift uses nine recovered objects under a declared GLORYS12/WAVERYS current, wave and object-response model. Drift maps condition each case on available model support before assigning the equal weights; omitted support is reported. Search likelihoods preserve footprint holes. ATSB detection values of 50%, 80% and 94% test uncertainty; 94% is an approximate reference derived from ATSB (2017), Figure 73, p.96. An approximate 2018 outline is tested separately at 60%, with shared or independent missed detections. Recent unlocalized coverage is unassessed.

Across the displayed aerodynamic models and numerical repeats, the drift-plus-ATSB94 mixture places 74–83% north of 35°S. The graphics show 50/90/99% probability contours, with 25 km display smoothing. Original weights determine probabilities. This range is sensitivity, not a confidence interval. Resampling copies candidates. The residual weights have the diversity of just 29–73 equally weighted ancestors; their descendants remain dependent. Omitting one original cruise run shifts some cumulative impact probabilities by up to 8 percentage points. Physical calibration and numerical convergence remain incomplete, so precise hotspots are provisional. A separate synthetic cruise-recovery test still fails. Aerodynamic alternatives remain separate. Future calibrated hydroacoustic likelihoods could similarly update locations and case weights; none is applied here.
conditions: Four joint final-BFO reliability states have equal 25% probabilities after their separate SATCOM fits and common airborne condition, before drift or search. These are declared mixture weights, not reliability probabilities inferred from incompatible dropped-observation normalizers.

All states retain the normally corrected R600 BTO and require computed impact no earlier than 00:19:37.443 UTC on 8 March 2014; this airborne-transmitter interpretation is common to all states. R1200 BTO is omitted. No extra warm-up offset is used.

Flight PDFs condition on computed impacts. Drift PDFs additionally condition each component on the available native drift domain before assigning equal weights. Unassessed mass is disclosed and is not evidence against a BFO state. Drift and search can then update state probabilities.

The same nine-object GLORYS12/WAVERYS drift likelihood is used across each mixture; no isotope or Australian coastal non-recovery term. Two cowling numerical estimates, two terminal seeds and two aerodynamic families are reported separately.
Search evidence uses the recorded geographic/detection sensitivities, preserving mapped holes and campaign overlap assumptions. Recent unlocalized search totals do not exclude any geographic cell.

Hydroacoustic observations are not included. A future calibrated acoustic likelihood could update both impact positions and conditional-model probabilities, using a common observation model and explicit non-detection treatment.

The 1,020,000 initial cruise candidates are not independent posterior draws. Cruise recovery, fuel/flight calibration and terminal/drift numerical convergence remain unresolved. Fuel exhaustion support remains 00:15–00:19 UTC.
